extraction.name: MathVista
extraction.description: MathVista is a benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks. It consists of 6,141 examples, derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). The benchmark covers seven mathematical reasoning types (algebraic, arithmetic, geometry, logical, numeric common sense, scientific, statistical) across five primary tasks (figure question answering, geometry problem solving, math word problem, textbook question answering, visual question answering) with diverse visual contexts including natural images, geometry diagrams, abstract scenes, synthetic scenes, charts, and plots.
extraction.creator: UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research Redmond
extraction.inLanguage: English (primarily); 6.57% non-English including Chinese and Persian
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MathVista was collected by (1) collecting 9 MathQA datasets in multimodal settings, (2) reviewing more than 70 VQA datasets and collecting 19 of them containing math-related instances, and (3) creating three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) to address missing types of mathematical reasoning. Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. Heuristic rules were designed to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning, followed by manual labeling by three expert annotators.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations. Due to the heterogeneity of these sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 math-targeted QA datasets and 19 VQA datasets) plus 3 newly created datasets (IQTest from online learning platforms puzzle test figures, FunctionQA with functional plots, PaperQA with academic paper figures sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: PaperQA sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface; overall dataset construction timeframe not explicitly stated
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automatic filtration using heuristic rules: examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words in the questions were selected. This yielded 4,949 VQA-format examples. Then three expert annotators manually labeled these to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning. Majority voting applied and each source dataset limited to 400 examples, finalizing 2,739 examples from VQA datasets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: All questions in the three newly created datasets were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process. A two-step process was used: initially each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers (inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2%). Discrepancies were resolved through team discussion. Metadata annotations include question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, and visual context. Expert annotators manually labeled mathematical reasoning categories for 1,000 examples to verify automatic annotation quality.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom GUI annotation tool (shown in Figures 22, 23, 24); Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) for human performance baseline and Bard assessment task
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement was measured using Fleiss Kappa score, yielding 0.775 indicating substantial consistency. For the newly collected 736 questions, only 6 exhibited disagreements in annotated answers (99.2% consistency rate). For automatic vs human mathematical reasoning annotation: 94.1% of examples had exact same set of reasoning types, with 98.79% of individual labels identical.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three reviewers per example for new datasets; five annotators per question for human performance evaluation on testmini
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields for new dataset annotation. For human performance baseline: Amazon Mechanical Turk annotators with satisfactory annotating history, passed qualification examples, possessing a high school degree or higher. Workers had history of completing more than 5,000 HIT tasks with acceptance score higher than 0.99.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 for answer extraction (>99.5% accuracy); EasyOCR for OCR text detection; Multimodal Bard for image caption generation
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: MathVista is divided into testmini (1,000 examples for model development validation) and test (5,141 examples for standard evaluation). Answer labels for test will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination, and an online evaluation platform will be maintained. The authors are committed to maintaining the datasets, refining potential data noise, and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark plays a critical role in the development of general-purpose AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks. Applications include solving complex problems in educational disciplines, helping analysts with logical queries about statistical data, and assisting in theorem proving and scientific discovery.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Dataset coverage limitations: there may be gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. The dataset's focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts (spanning specific domains like science and college-level math) necessitates a more labor-intensive collection process. Scalability and generalizability to other domains remain a concern. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations, and due to heterogeneity of sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure. The study focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models given the rapid development in foundation models.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation benchmark for assessing mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models (LLMs and LMMs) in visual contexts. Used for Testing and Validation. The testmini subset (1,000 examples) is intended for model development validation or for those with limited computing resources. The test subset (5,141 examples) is for standard evaluation.
